parameters.content:
## Send one WhatsApp alert for the messages that need an answer today

### Who is it for
Anyone whose work arrives on four or five accounts at once and who has stopped reading the notifications because there are too many of them: founders, freelancers, recruiters, sales, support.

### How it works
Two Nilyo triggers listen at the same time: `message.new` on LinkedIn, Instagram, Telegram and WhatsApp, and `email.new` on Gmail, Outlook or any IMAP mailbox. A Code node turns those two very different payloads into one shape, because a Message and an Email are not the same object: the Message carries the text, the chat and the direction, while the email carries a whole Email whose `from` is an array and which has no id to read back.

Then the workflow earns the interruption. Anything you sent yourself, or that the provider did not classify as inbound, stops there. For a conversation it reads the last messages: if you answered last, nothing is sent, because a follow-up to your own reply is not something waiting on you. An email is judged on its own payload, which is already complete. Only then does the model see the new message with its conversation and answer whether it needs you today, and why in a few words.

The last guard is the clock. An urgent message at three in the morning is still not worth a phone buzzing: the alert is held until the end of your quiet hours, never dropped. What arrives on WhatsApp is one line per thing that actually waits on you, with the channel, the person and the reason.

### How to set up
1. Create a personal token in Nilyo (Agent access) and store it in a **Nilyo API** credential.
2. Connect in Nilyo the accounts you want watched, and the WhatsApp that receives the alerts.
3. In **Settings**, set the recipient, your timezone and your quiet hours.
4. Add your OpenAI credential to the triage node, then publish the workflow to register both subscriptions.

### Requirements
A Nilyo account with at least one messaging or email account connected plus WhatsApp, and an OpenAI account.

### How to customize
Narrow the triggers to the accounts that matter, change the definition of urgent in the prompt, widen or switch off the quiet hours by setting the same start and end, or send the alert to Slack or Telegram instead.

### Community node
This template uses the **Nilyo** community node (`n8n-nodes-nilyo`), verified by n8n. On n8n Cloud, enable Verified Community Nodes in the Admin Panel and add Nilyo from the canvas. On self-hosted n8n, install `n8n-nodes-nilyo` from Settings > Community nodes.

## 1. Two accounts families, one workflow

One trigger for conversations (LinkedIn, Instagram, Telegram, WhatsApp), one for mailboxes (Gmail, Outlook, IMAP). **Settings** holds the recipient, your timezone and the hours you do not want to be disturbed.

## 2. One shape for two very different events

`message.new` carries a Message; `email.new` carries an Email whose `from` is an array and which has no id to read back. Everything after this node reads one normalized item. A message you sent, or one the provider did not classify, never gets past **Inbound only**.

## 3. Read before deciding to interrupt

A conversation is read first: if you answered last, nothing is sent, because a reply to your own message is not waiting on you. An email is judged on its payload, which is already complete. A conversation that cannot be read still alerts, and says so, rather than being treated as empty.

## 4. Does it need you today

The model sees the new message with its conversation, and answers with one small JSON object: urgent or not, and why in a few words. A third follow-up on the same question is urgent; a thank-you after your answer is not.

## 5. Not at three in the morning

Inside your quiet hours the alert is held until they end, never dropped. Set the same start and end to switch this off.

## 6. One line, on WhatsApp

The channel, the person, the reason, and a note when the alert was held or judged without its conversation.
